answer: Proof-of-work makes every identity cost real computation: to register, an agent must burn cycles on a puzzle whose difficulty rises with each identity it already holds. A farmer running ten thousand sock puppets faces a bill at the zenith of his operation: each puppet needs its own GPU hours, and the expense climbs in a spiral that devours any reward the seats would earn. A botnet driven by one relic server collapses here, since a single machine cannot grind puzzles for thousands of puppets before the epoch closes. The defense is pricing, not trust: faking many voices stops being free.
